q: Fill in the blank: Priya is not only intelligent ___ hardworking.
exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: not only ... but also। सही वाक्य: "Priya is not only intelligent but also hardworking."
📌 दोनों भागों के बाद समान part of speech हो (parallelism): intelligent ... hardworking।
✖ as well as — 'not only' का जोड़ा नहीं है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। and — समान विचारों को जोड़ता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। and also — 'not only' का सही जोड़ा नहीं है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Correlative pair: not only ... but also. Correct: "Priya is not only intelligent but also hardworking."
📌 Both parts should be followed by the same part of speech (parallelism): intelligent ... hardworking (adjectives).
✖ as well as — is not the partner of 'not only'; does not fit here. and — joins similar ideas (addition); does not fit here. and also — is not the correlative partner of 'not only'; does not fit here.

q: Fill in the blank: We went trekking in ___ Aravallis.
exp:
✔ पर्वत-श्रेणियों के नाम से पहले 'the': the Aravallis, the Himalayas, the Vindhyas। सही वाक्य: "We went trekking in the Aravallis."
📌 अकेली चोटी के साथ article नहीं: Mount Everest।
✖ no article — अकेली चोटी के लिए, श्रेणी के लिए नहीं। a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं।
expe:
✔ Mountain ranges (plural names) take 'the': the Aravallis, the Himalayas, the Vindhyas. Correct: "We went trekking in the Aravallis."
📌 Single peaks take no article: Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga.
✖ no article — used for single peaks, not ranges. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here.

q: Fill in the blank: Meena succeeded ___ passing the exam.
exp:
✔ सही collocation 'succeed in' है। 'Succeed' के बाद 'in' + noun/-ing आता है। सही वाक्य: "Meena succeeded in passing the exam."
📌 इसी तरह: persist in, indulge in, engaged in.
✖ on — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'rely on, insist on' में। at — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'good at, look at' में। with — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'agree with (person), cope with' में।
expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'succeed in'. 'Succeed in' + noun/-ing (passing). Correct: "Meena succeeded in passing the exam."
📌 Similar: persist in, indulge in, engaged in.
✖ on — wrong here; used in e.g. 'rely on, insist on'. at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'. with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'.

q: Fill in the blank: Both Asha ___ Kavita are teachers.
exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: both ... and; verb plural (are) होती है। सही वाक्य: "Both Asha and Kavita are teachers."
📌 'Both...as well as' गलत है। अन्य: either...or, neither...nor।
✖ nor — केवल 'neither' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। as well as — 'both ... as well as' गलत है; 'both' का जोड़ा 'and' है। or — 'either' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Correlative pair: both ... and; the verb is plural (are). Correct: "Both Asha and Kavita are teachers."
📌 'Both...as well as' is wrong. Other pairs: either...or, neither...nor.
✖ nor — pairs only with 'neither'; does not fit here. as well as — 'both ... as well as' is incorrect; 'both' pairs with 'and'. or — pairs with 'either'; does not fit here.

q: Fill in the blank: Camels are used for travel in ___ Gobi Desert.
exp:
✔ मरुस्थलों के नाम से पहले 'the': the Thar Desert, the Gobi, the Sahara। सही वाक्य: "Camels are used for travel in the Gobi Desert."
📌 नदियों, महासागरों और पर्वत-श्रेणियों (the Himalayas) के साथ भी 'the'।
✖ a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। no article — मरुस्थल के नाम के साथ 'the' आवश्यक।
expe:
✔ Names of deserts take 'the': the Thar Desert, the Gobi Desert, the Sahara. Correct: "Camels are used for travel in the Gobi Desert."
📌 'The' also with rivers, oceans and mountain ranges (the Himalayas).
✖ a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. no article — desert names need 'the'.

q: Fill in the blank: Anil replied ___ my letter.
exp:
✔ सही collocation 'reply to' है। 'Reply' के बाद 'to' आता है: reply to a letter. सही वाक्य: "Anil replied to my letter."
📌 'Answer' के साथ preposition नहीं: answer a letter.
✖ at — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'good at, look at' में। of — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'jealous of, aware of' में। for — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'famous for, eligible for' में।
expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'reply to'. 'Reply' (verb) takes 'to': reply to a letter. Correct: "Anil replied to my letter."
📌 'Answer' needs no preposition: answer a letter.
✖ at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'. of — wrong here; used in e.g. 'jealous of, aware of'. for — wrong here; used in e.g. 'famous for, eligible for'.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither Kishore ___ Deepak came to the party.
exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: neither ... nor (न यह, न वह)। सही वाक्य: "Neither Kishore nor Deepak came to the party."
📌 जोड़े: either...or, both...and, not only...but also।
✖ but — विरोध (contrast) बताता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। and — समान विचारों को जोड़ता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। or — 'either' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Correlative pair: neither ... nor (not one and not the other). Correct: "Neither Kishore nor Deepak came to the party."
📌 Pairs: either...or, both...and, not only...but also.
✖ but — shows contrast; does not fit here. and — joins similar ideas (addition); does not fit here. or — pairs with 'either'; does not fit here.

q: Fill in the blank: Kishore was born in ___ May.
exp:
✔ महीनों और दिनों के नाम से पहले article नहीं लगता: in June, on Monday। सही वाक्य: "Kishore was born in May."
📌 Preposition: in + month/year; on + day/date (on Monday)।
✖ a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। the — सामान्यतः महीने के नाम से पहले नहीं।
expe:
✔ Names of months (and days) take no article: in June, on Monday. Correct: "Kishore was born in May."
📌 Prepositions: in + month/year (in June, in 1990); on + day/date (on Monday, on 5 June).
✖ a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. the — not used before a month name in general.

q: Fill in the blank: Gopal speaks ___ German fluently.

q: Fill in the blank: Mohan has lived here ___ 2005.
exp:
✔ Present perfect में किसी समय-बिंदु (वर्ष/दिन) के साथ 'since' आता है। सही वाक्य: "Mohan has lived here since 2005."
📌 समय-अवधि के साथ 'for' (for ten years)।
✖ from — 'to/till' के साथ (from 9 to 5); यहाँ present perfect के साथ नहीं। in — simple past के साथ (in 1995), present perfect के साथ नहीं। for — अवधि के साथ आता है, समय-बिंदु के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'Since' + a point of time (a year/day) with the present perfect (continuous). Correct: "Mohan has lived here since 2005."
📌 'For' + a period of time (for ten years, for two hours).
✖ from — needs 'to/till' (from 9 to 5); not with present perfect here. in — for a point in past (in 1995) with simple past, not present perfect. for — needs a period of time, not a point.

q: Fill in the blank: Mohan has gone to ___ Bhutan.
exp:
✔ अधिकांश देशों के नाम (Japan, Nepal, France...) proper noun हैं; इनसे पहले article नहीं लगता। सही वाक्य: "Mohan has gone to Bhutan."
📌 बहुवचन या Republic/Kingdom/States वाले नामों में 'the': the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives।
✖ an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। the — केवल the USA, the UK, the Netherlands जैसे नामों में। a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं।
expe:
✔ Names of most countries (Japan, Nepal, France...) are proper nouns and take no article. Correct: "Mohan has gone to Bhutan."
📌 'The' is used with country names that are plural or contain Republic/Kingdom/States: the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives.
✖ an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. the — only for names like the USA, the UK, the Netherlands. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here.

✔ The correct collocation is 'jealous of'. 'Jealous' is always followed by 'of'. Correct: "The farmer is jealous of his neighbour's success."
📌 Similar: envious of, proud of, afraid of, fond of.
✖ at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'. with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'. from — wrong here; used in e.g. 'suffer from, abstain from'.

expe:

✖ then — is an adverb of time, not a correlative with hardly/no sooner; does not fit here. that — introduces a clause; pairs with 'so/such'; does not fit here. than — is used after comparatives and with 'no sooner'; does not fit here.

✔ 'accustomed to' = किसी चीज़ का आदी — accustomed to hard work; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसके बाद noun/gerund आता है। सही वाक्य: Sunita is accustomed to hard work.
📌 इसी तरह: used to, addicted to, habituated to।
✖ with/for/of — 'accustomed' के साथ ये prepositions मानक प्रयोग में नहीं आते; सही collocation 'accustomed to' है।
expe:
✔ 'Accustomed to' means used to; 'to' is a preposition here, so it takes a noun/gerund: accustomed to hard work / to working hard. Correct sentence: Sunita is accustomed to hard work.
📌 Similarly: used to, addicted to, habituated to.
✖ with/for/of — not idiomatic with 'accustomed'; the correct collocation is 'accustomed to'.

q: In which option is the article used correctly?
exp:
✔ 'a ewe' सही है — ewe (भेड़) का उच्चारण 'यू' — 'य' (consonant sound) से शुरू, इसलिए 'a'।
📌 a/an का चयन spelling से नहीं, उच्चारण (sound) से होता है: vowel sound → an (an hour, an MLA), consonant sound → a (a uniform, a one-rupee coin)।
✖ A) 'an one-rupee coin' गलत → 'a one-rupee coin' (one का उच्चारण 'वन' है, जो 'व' (consonant sound) से शुरू होता है)। C) 'a hour' गलत → 'an hour' (h silent है, उच्चारण 'आवर' (vowel sound))। D) 'a heir' गलत → 'an heir' (h silent है, उच्चारण 'एयर' (vowel sound))।
expe:
✔ 'a ewe' is correct — 'ewe' (female sheep) is pronounced 'you', beginning with the consonant sound 'y', so 'a'.
📌 a/an depends on the first sound, not the spelling: vowel sound → an (an hour, an MLA); consonant sound → a (a uniform, a one-rupee coin).
✖ A) 'an one-rupee coin' is wrong → 'a one-rupee coin' ('one' is pronounced 'wun', beginning with the consonant sound 'w'). C) 'a hour' is wrong → 'an hour' (the 'h' is silent; it begins with the vowel sound 'our'). D) 'a heir' is wrong → 'an heir' (the 'h' is silent; it sounds like 'air' (vowel sound)).

q: Fill in the blank: Sunita is anxious ___ her son's health.
exp:
✔ 'anxious about' = किसी बात को लेकर चिंतित — anxious about her son's health। सही वाक्य: Sunita is anxious about her son's health.
📌 'anxious for' = किसी चीज़ को पाने के लिए उत्सुक (anxious for success); 'anxious to + verb' = उत्सुक (anxious to meet you)।
✖ with/at/of — 'anxious' के साथ ये prepositions मानक प्रयोग में नहीं आते; सही collocation 'anxious about' है।
expe:
✔ 'Anxious about' means worried about something: anxious about her son's health. Correct sentence: Sunita is anxious about her son's health.
📌 'Anxious for' = eager for (anxious for success); 'anxious to + verb' = eager to (anxious to meet you).
✖ with/at/of — not idiomatic with 'anxious'; the correct collocation is 'anxious about'.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish must finish the work ___ Monday.
exp:
✔ 'by' = किसी समय-सीमा तक (deadline) — finish the work by Monday (सोमवार तक/से पहले पूरा)। सही वाक्य: Harish must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'till/until' निरंतरता बताता है: I will wait till Monday; 'since' perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल के बिंदु से: since Monday।
✖ for — अवधि के लिए (for two days); till — क्रिया जारी रहने के लिए, deadline के लिए नहीं; since — perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल से अब तक।
expe:
✔ 'By' marks a deadline: finish the work by Monday (on or before Monday). Correct sentence: Harish must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'Till/until' shows continuation (wait till Monday); 'since' is used with perfect tenses from a past point (since Monday).
✖ for — a period (for two days); till — continuation, not a deadline; since — from a past point, with perfect tenses.

q: Fill in the blank: Vijay was absent ___ account of illness.
exp:
✔ 'on account of' (के कारण) fixed phrase है — absent on account of illness। सही वाक्य: Vijay was absent on account of illness.
📌 समानार्थी: because of, owing to, due to।
✖ in/for/by — 'on account of' fixed phrase है, इसमें दूसरा preposition नहीं आता (absent from = अनुपस्थित 'से', जैसे absent from school)।
expe:
✔ 'On account of' (= because of) is a fixed phrase: absent on account of illness. Correct sentence: Vijay was absent on account of illness.
📌 Synonyms: because of, owing to, due to.
✖ in/for/by — 'on account of' is a fixed phrase and takes no other preposition ('absent from' is used for the place: absent from school).

expe:
✔ 'a NCC cadet' is incorrect; the correct form is 'an NCC cadet' — 'N' is pronounced 'en', which begins with a vowel sound.
📌 a/an depends on the first sound, not the spelling: vowel sound → an (an hour, an MLA); consonant sound → a (a uniform, a one-rupee coin).
✖ A) 'a Union Minister' is correct — 'Union' is pronounced 'yoo-nion', beginning with the consonant sound 'y'. C) 'a university' is correct — it is pronounced 'yoo-niversity', beginning with the consonant sound 'y'. D) 'an MLA' is correct — 'M' is pronounced 'em', which begins with a vowel sound.

q: Fill in the blank: Sanjay has no friends ___ Manoj.
exp:
✔ 'besides' = के अलावा (in addition to/except) — no friends besides Manoj (मनोज के अलावा कोई मित्र नहीं)। सही वाक्य: Sanjay has no friends besides Manoj.
📌 'beside' = के पास/बगल में: sat beside her। एक 's' से अर्थ बदल जाता है।
✖ beside — 'के पास'; between — दो के बीच; among — दो से अधिक के बीच — अर्थ नहीं बनता।
expe:
✔ 'Besides' means apart from/in addition to: no friends besides him. Correct sentence: Sanjay has no friends besides Manoj.
📌 'Beside' means next to: sat beside her. One 's' changes the meaning.
✖ beside — 'next to'; between — for two; among — for more than two — none gives the sense 'apart from'.

q: Fill in the blank: Divya must finish the work ___ Monday.
exp:
✔ 'by' = किसी समय-सीमा तक (deadline) — finish the work by Monday (सोमवार तक/से पहले पूरा)। सही वाक्य: Divya must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'till/until' निरंतरता बताता है: I will wait till Monday; 'since' perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल के बिंदु से: since Monday।
✖ for — अवधि के लिए (for two days); till — क्रिया जारी रहने के लिए, deadline के लिए नहीं; since — perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल से अब तक।
expe:
✔ 'By' marks a deadline: finish the work by Monday (on or before Monday). Correct sentence: Divya must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'Till/until' shows continuation (wait till Monday); 'since' is used with perfect tenses from a past point (since Monday).
✖ for — a period (for two days); till — continuation, not a deadline; since — from a past point, with perfect tenses.

✔ 'an hour' सही है — h silent है, उच्चारण 'आवर' (vowel sound), इसलिए 'an'।
📌 a/an का चयन spelling से नहीं, उच्चारण (sound) से होता है: vowel sound → an (an hour, an MLA), consonant sound → a (a uniform, a one-rupee coin)।
✖ A) 'a SP' गलत → 'an SP' (S का उच्चारण 'एस' (vowel sound) है)। C) 'an European' गलत → 'a European' (उच्चारण 'यूरोपियन' — 'य' (consonant sound) से शुरू)। D) 'a M.A. degree' गलत → 'an M.A. degree' (M का उच्चारण 'एम' (vowel sound) है)।
expe:
✔ 'an hour' is correct — the 'h' is silent; it begins with the vowel sound 'our', so 'an'.
📌 a/an depends on the first sound, not the spelling: vowel sound → an (an hour, an MLA); consonant sound → a (a uniform, a one-rupee coin).
✖ A) 'a SP' is wrong → 'an SP' ('S' is pronounced 'es', which begins with a vowel sound). C) 'an European' is wrong → 'a European' ('European' is pronounced 'yoo-ropean', beginning with the consonant sound 'y'). D) 'a M.A. degree' is wrong → 'an M.A. degree' ('M' is pronounced 'em', which begins with a vowel sound).

q: Fill in the blank: Arjun must finish the work ___ Monday.
exp:
✔ 'by' = किसी समय-सीमा तक (deadline) — finish the work by Monday (सोमवार तक/से पहले पूरा)। सही वाक्य: Arjun must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'till/until' निरंतरता बताता है: I will wait till Monday; 'since' perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल के बिंदु से: since Monday।
✖ for — अवधि के लिए (for two days); till — क्रिया जारी रहने के लिए, deadline के लिए नहीं; since — perfect tense के साथ भूतकाल से अब तक।
expe:
✔ 'By' marks a deadline: finish the work by Monday (on or before Monday). Correct sentence: Arjun must finish the work by Monday.
📌 'Till/until' shows continuation (wait till Monday); 'since' is used with perfect tenses from a past point (since Monday).
✖ for — a period (for two days); till — continuation, not a deadline; since — from a past point, with perfect tenses.
